Good evening, Chair, Mayor, and members of Council.
My name is Eric Schneider, and I'm a Senior Planner at the City.
I'm here tonight to make a recommendation for approval of a Zoning Bylaw Amendment
to facilitate a low-rise residential development.
As we advance to the next slide, I will discuss the site context of the lands.
The lands are comprised of three blocks, with block one fronting Blair Creek Drive
and blocks two and three fronting Blair Valley Street.
The lands have not yet been assigned municipal addresses or split into individual parcels for separate ownership.
These are known as lotless blocks.
The lands are on the north side of New Dundee Road, south of Blair Creek Drive, and are part of the Stauffer Woods Harvest Park subdivision, which is currently under development.
The lands are currently vacant.
On this slide, I will discuss the proposed concept.
The three blocks are proposed to be developed with 67 street-fronting townhouse units within 12 townhouse buildings.
Each townhouse dwelling would have an attached garage and a single car driveway.
Blocks one and three are adjacent to the large rectangular parcel on the corner, which is a future neighbourhood park of approximately one hectare in size.
The next slide illustrates the proposed zoning bylaw.
amendment. The amendment would add a site-specific provision that includes site-specific development
standards for reduced lot width on external units and to allow townhouse blocks of six
rather than four. The three parcels affected are shown as area one on the map.
In regards to water capacity, the region provided comments stating that the proposal does not
increase the overall number of units contemplated through the existing service agreement for
these stages of the Stauffer Woods subdivision and therefore has no objection to this application.
Next I will briefly summarize the opportunity in this application.
The opportunity to create 67 new townhouse dwelling units in a low rise building form
and to allow for appropriate development within this planned greenfield subdivision that is
draft approved and registered, to contribute to the diversity of housing within the Dune
South neighbourhood. In summary, the proposed site-specific provision will facilitate a new
low-rise development and the proposed application represents good planning principles and is
consistent with provincial, regional and the City's planning policies.
